chunks: There is no adhan, no iqamah, no Jumu'ah, no touching of the Stone, no entering the Ka'bah, no running between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and no shaving upon women; rather, they shorten from their hair.

key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: the call announcing the commencement of prayer
key_terms.اسْتِلَامُ الْحَجَرِ: touching or greeting the Black Stone during hajj rites
key_terms.الْحَلْقُ: shaving the head in pilgrimage rites
key_terms.الْهَرْوَلَةُ: brisk movement between al-Safa and al-Marwah

ai.seo_question: What ritual duties are not required of women in salat and hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a set of legal rulings specific to women regarding certain ritual acts in salat and hajj. It clarifies that these acts are not required of them, and that in place of shaving the head, they shorten their hair.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.908 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"There is no adhan (call to prayer), iqamah (call to commence prayer), Jumu'ah (Jumu’ah prayer), touching of the Black Stone, entry into the Kaaba, or running (between the hills of Safa and Marwa) required for women, nor is shaving (the head during pilgrimage). Rather, they may shorten (cut) their hair."
